properties.description:
Given a filesystem path to a design store, report which design is there — its stable graph id, its label, whether that identity was minted or adopted, and the schema stamp the store carries — WITHOUT opening it, locking it, or writing anything. The paired half of discovery: the agent walks the tree and finds `.reflow2` directories (file navigation, which reflow2 does not do), and this answers what each one IS, so a person can be shown a menu before anything is created.

WHAT IT PREVENTS, measured: a session at the root of `hxm_program` was told "this directory has no design yet" and minted a THIRD graph while two populated ones sat one and two directories down. The agent could have listed the paths; nothing could say what they were.

BUILT 2026-08-05 as `describe_designs`, served on BOTH the full surface and the LATENT (no-design) surface — the latter deliberately, because a session with no design is the exact moment someone is about to create one, and a discovery tool only reachable after a design exists would arrive too late. Takes a LIST of paths, because the caller is sweeping a tree and one round trip per candidate is the wrong shape for a menu.

⭐ TWO DEVIATIONS FROM `dec:describe-a-design-without-binding-to-it`, BOTH FORCED BY THE CODE AND BOTH IMPROVEMENTS ON WHAT WAS ASKED FOR.

(1) NO NODE COUNTS. The decision said the report would carry "node counts by type". It cannot, and the reason is the whole design: `DesignGraph::open_rocksdb_with_provenance` WRITES `<path>.meta.json` via `check_and_stamp` and MINTS `<path>.id.json` via `identity::resolve` when the store has none. So counting would mean opening, and opening an unnamed store would NAME IT — inspecting a design would create the thing it was asked to look for. Identity and stamp answer *which design is this and how old is its schema*, which is what choosing between designs actually needs; size is not worth minting an identity to get.

(2) NO `busy` STATE, AND IT IS NOT MISSING. The decision flagged "must distinguish busy from absent" because a store held by a running server is exclusively locked. That turned out to be MOOT: everything reported comes from the two sidecar files beside the store, so nothing is ever locked and a design another session is writing right now describes perfectly. The requirement was met by removing the condition rather than by handling it.

THE STATES IT DOES REPORT, and the distinction that carries the value: `design` (named from its sidecar), `unnamed` (something is there whose identity cannot be read without opening — reported as such rather than named by the act of asking), `opted_in` (directory exists, nothing written yet), `absent` (nothing here). SOMETHING-UNNAMED MUST NEVER READ AS NOTHING-HERE, because "no design here" is the sentence that starts an unwanted one. Every row also carries a plain-language `reading`, because a bare enum makes the caller invent the meaning.

SHIPPED WITH THE INSTRUCTION THAT MAKES ANYONE CALL IT. `reflow2_start_design`'s description previously ended "it is safe to call when unsure" with no mention of looking around — the sentence behind the accident. It now requires a nearby sweep first and says why, and its payload tells a caller who skipped the check to say so immediately, while the recovery is still a deletion rather than a merge. A tool no skill tells anyone to use is this project's own recurring defect ([BL-152], [BL-178], [BL-197], [BL-204]); shipping the tool without the instruction would have been the fifth.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE: how a session is then POINTED at the chosen design (`dec:how-a-session-is-pointed-at-a-design`, open — with `dec:pointing-a-session-is-project-scope-only` as the working field answer).
properties.name: Say what design lives at a path, without binding to it
